title: Exploit Chain: Persistent Session Hijacking via Token Exposure + No Rotation + No Revocation + IDOR
description: Step 1: Attacker obtains refresh_token from POST /api/v1/auth/login response (finding-028, CWE-200). Step 2: Refresh token never rotates on use (finding-033, CWE-613) - stolen token remains valid indefinitely. Step 3: Even if token is revoked, vulnerableAuth middleware does not check revocation (finding-030, CWE-306). Step 4: Attacker uses valid/stolen refresh token to obtain access tokens and access IDOR endpoints (finding-007,008,009,010 - CWE-639) to access cross-user data (customers, appointments, barbers).
impact: Full persistent session hijacking with cross-user data access. Attacker can maintain indefinite access to any user account and exfiltrate all customer, appointment, and barber data without detection.
mitigation: 1) Remove refresh_token from login response body; use secure HttpOnly cookies. 2) Implement refresh token rotation (revoke old, issue new). 3) Add revocation check in authentication middleware. 4) Add ownership verification in all resource endpoints.

history.details: Constructed by chaining findings finding-028, finding-033, finding-030, finding-007, finding-008, finding-009, finding-010.
